name: Order and ticket edits
description: Change an order's buyer details, resend its receipt, check a whole order out at the door, and correct a ticket's attendee name, the same as in the dashboard (Orders): each write runs as the member who created the key, needs that member's role (owner or manager), and is kept in the order's edit history. Prices, quantities, tickets and who holds them never change through these: refund or reissue for that, and a ticket changes hands only by transfer (its barcode rotates). Also a dry run of a guest-list import. Opendate's /v1/confirms/:event_id/orders/:id, …/send_receipt, …/check_out, /v1/confirms/:event_id/tickets/:barcode and /v1/confirms/:id/guest_list_preview answer too. Bodies may be JSON or form-encoded, flat or wrapped (`order[first_name]`, `ticket[attendee_name]`).

endpoints.description: Sets the buyer's first and last name, contact email, phone number and notes. Only those: anything else (amounts, quantity, ticket type, status) answers 400. The email is where receipts and order mail go; the tickets, their holders and the invoice stay as they were. Sending the current values changes nothing and records nothing. Receipts keep going to the address the order was placed with unless the organization allows other addresses.

endpoints.description: Mails the order's receipt again (what was paid, the lines, the all-in price note) through the normal outbox. It never contains ticket claim links. To the address the order was placed with. Any other address, including a contact email changed with PUT /v1/orders/:id, is an override: allowed (and then the default) only when an owner has allowed other addresses for the organization (Orders, Settings); otherwise the receipt still goes to the original address, and asking for another one answers 403. At most 3 an hour per order by default (an owner can raise it to 10) and 10 a day. Also /v1/orders/:id/send_receipt.

endpoints.description: The opposite of checking the order in: records an exit for every ticket of the order that is inside on a re-entry check-in list (the last scan there was an entry), the same as at the door, so re-entry and the live headcount stay right. A ticket that is already out records nothing and answers not-inside, so calling it again is safe. Tickets the order no longer holds (transferred away) are skipped. A ticket checked in on the event's default list can't be checked out (exit-not-allowed): exits need a re-entry list. A typed exit is a door override, so the key's creator must be an owner or manager. Also /v1/orders/:id/check_out.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The order's id (its checkout session id). One of another organization answers 404. Also answers under /v1/confirms/:event_id/orders/:id, where the order must be on that event.

parameters.name: list_id
parameters.description: Only this check-in list (gate). Default: every re-entry list the ticket is inside on.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Kept on each exit (default "order check-out").

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: A label for the app (shown in the check-in log).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Optional. 8-100 letters, digits, _ . : or -. Resending a write with the same key replays the first answer (with "idempotent_replay": true) instead of doing it again; the same key on another action or target, or with a different body, answers 400.

responses.description: Per ticket: changed true when an exit was recorded.

endpoints.description: Sets or clears the attendee name on a ticket (attendee_name, or first_name and last_name). Changing who holds the ticket is a transfer, not an edit: the barcode rotates and transfer rules apply, so an email other than the holder's answers 409 (the holder sends it from their ticket). The holder's own email is accepted and changes nothing. Not for a ticket in transfer or voided. Also /v1/confirms/:event_id/tickets/:barcode.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ticket's id, or a door code (T-…) of it. One of another organization answers 404.

endpoints.description: Checks an import without adding anyone. Send one of: text (pasted names, one per line; +2, (+2), plus 2 or x2 after a name adds plus-ones; bullets and numbering are dropped; lines ending in : ! or ?, lines with an @ and lines over six words are skipped), csv (an attendee export, read like the dashboard's Door import: Eventbrite, Posh, DICE, Shotgun, RA or any sheet with a name column) or rows. Each row comes back ready, duplicate (already on a list of the event, or earlier in this import), invalid (no name, code too long) or too_many_plus_ones, with warnings for malformed emails (the import drops them). capacity says what the import would do to the list's cap and, when the list counts toward capacity, to the event's. Writes nothing. Also /v1/events/:id/guest_list_preview and /v1/confirms/:id/guest_list_preview. Bodies up to 2.25 MB.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The event's id. One of another organization answers 404.

parameters.name: list_id
parameters.description: The guest list it would go into (its cap and plus-one limit apply). `guest_list_id` works too.

parameters.name: text
parameters.description: Pasted names, one per line.

parameters.name: csv
parameters.description: An attendee export as CSV text (comma, semicolon or tab).

parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Rows of { name, email?, phone?, code?, ticket?, note?, plus_ones? }, at most 5000.

Tessa
Ann Lee

responses.description: What the import would do.
None or more than one of text, csv and rows; a CSV with no rows; over 5000 rows.

example.error: send one of text (pasted names), csv (an attendee export) or rows.
